extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, practitioners, assignees, and patent attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for establishing, asserting, maintaining, correcting, and refunding U.S. USPTO small entity (fee reduction) status in patent applications and patents, including who may sign or pay to assert status and the procedural requirements and consequences.  Covers assertions by writing or by payment, investigation duties, refunds, corrections, and loss of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status may be established by the submission of a simple written assertion of entitlement to small entity status; the assertion must be signed, clearly identifiable, and convey the concept of entitlement to small entity status (37 CFR 1.27(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No particular form is required; written assertions or references to small entity fees will be liberally interpreted. The written assertion can be made in any paper filed in or with the application and may be as little as a simple sentence or a checked box on an application transmittal letter. Practitioners may continue to use former USPTO forms for educational purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties who can assert and sign (by writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties permitted by 37 CFR 1.33(b) to file a paper in an application (including a registered practitioner) may assert entitlement; additionally, one of the individuals identified as an inventor, or a partial assignee, can also sign the written assertion (37 CFR 1.27(c)(2)(i)-(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: of three pro se inventors, one inventor upon filing may submit a written assertion and establish small entity status. Any inventor identified on filing (e.g., in a transmittal letter) but not yet named by executed oath/declaration may submit a written assertion; an actual inventor who has not been identified on filing may not file a written assertion. See 37 CFR 1.41(a)(1), 1.63, 1.4(d), 10.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a signed written assertion (filing vs signing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although several inventors may sign or assert, there is a distinction as to who can file a written assertion once signed: 37 CFR 1.27(c)(2)(ii) and 1.33(b) permit one of several inventors to file as well as to sign, but a partial assignee may sign yet the written assertion must be filed by an appropriate party under 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, a partial assignee cannot both sign and independently file the assertion unless the filer is authorized under 1.33(b). See paragraph III for filing limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by payment of exact small entity basic filing or basic national fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of an exact small entity basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a)-(e)) or basic national fee (37 CFR 1.492(a)) is considered a sufficient assertion of entitlement to small entity status (37 CFR 1.27(c)(3)). An applicant paying the exact small entity basic filing or basic national fee automatically establishes small entity status for the application even without any other assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This payment-based assertion acts as a safety net to avoid financial loss. Payment of a small entity fee other than a small entity basic filing or basic national fee (e.g., extension of time fee or issue fee) without a written assertion is not sufficient. If the wrong type of small entity fee type is selected but the exact amount is paid (e.g., design fee for a utility), small entity status is accorded, though applicant must still pay the correct small entity amount if selection causes a deficiency. If the amount paid is not the exact small entity fee required and no written assertion is present, small entity status will not be accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties who can assert by payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where small entity status is sought by payment of the basic filing or basic national fee, any party (including a third party) may submit payment (e.g., by check) and small entity status will be accorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment by a third party is treated as an assertion; however, payment must be of the exact small entity basic filing or basic national fee to establish status automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to file a written assertion even when paying fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though payment of the exact small entity basic filing or basic national fee can establish status, the Office encourages applicants to also file a written assertion of small entity status as well as pay the exact amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written assertion will provide small entity status should applicant fail to pay the exact amount. Application transmittal forms include a checkbox for submitting a written assertion. The payment-based provision is intended only as a safety net.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to investigate before asserting small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must do a complete and thorough investigation of all facts and circumstances before making a determination of actual entitlement to small entity status (37 CFR 1.27(f)). Where entitlement is uncertain, it should not be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should include review of whether a business is a 'small business concern' under section 3 of the Small Business Act and relevant SBA size standards (13 CFR 121.801–121.805). If rights have been assigned/licensed or are shared with other entities, review each related entity. For multiple inventors, check with co-inventors before one asserts status. The person asserting has a duty to investigate and self-certify unequivocally. The USPTO will not provide advisory opinions as to qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued obligations — re-determinations at issue and maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Once small entity status has been established in an application or patent, a new determination of entitlement is needed when the issue fee is due and when any maintenance fee is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entity status may be continued without regard to intermediate changes until those fee events, but the applicant must reassess entitlement at each such event. Costs of investigations may outweigh benefits; in some cases filing as non-small may be preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of status and required notification of loss
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.27(g)(1)-(2): Once established, small entity status may be paid without regard to change in status until the issue fee or any maintenance fee is due. Notification of any change resulting in loss of entitlement must be filed prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest of the issue fee or any maintenance fee due after the date on which status is no longer appropriate; the notification must be a specific written assertion (not merely payment of a non-small fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: On PTOL-85 Part B (Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due), applicants should (A) check the appropriate box indicating a change in entity status and (B) pay the non-small entity fee amount. Simply crossing out recitations or paying non-small fee without written notification is insufficient. See paragraph VII and X for correcting errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improperly establishing small entity status (fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt to fraudulently establish status as a small entity or to pay fees as a small entity with intent to deceive will be considered a fraud practiced or attempted on the Office (37 CFR 1.27(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office normally will not question a claim to status, but applicants should not rely on oral advice from Office employees about entitlement. Fraudulent assertions carry severe consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds based on later establishment of small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Refunds pursuant to 37 CFR 1.26 and 1.28: A refund based on later establishment of small entity status of portion of fees timely paid in full prior to establishing status may be obtained only if an assertion under 37 CFR 1.27(c) and a request for refund are filed within three months of the date of the timely payment of the full fee (37 CFR 1.28(a)). The three-month period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month refund period starts on the date the full fee was paid. Payment by authorization to charge a deposit account is treated as paid on date of receipt in the Office. If mailed with Certificate of Mailing, the three-month period starts on actual date of receipt. For Express Mail under 37 CFR 1.10, the Express Mail deposit date is the date of receipt for refund purposes. Refund requests and assertions should be addressed to Mail Stop 16, Director of the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting errors in small entity status — excusing good faith errors (37 CFR 1.28(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status and payment of small entity fees were established in good faith but later discovered to have been established in error or the Office was not notified of loss of entitlement, the error will be excused upon compliance with specific submission, itemization, and deficiency payment requirements (37 CFR 1.28(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (1) Separate submission limited to one application or patent per paper (§1.28(c)(1)); (2) Payment of the deficiency owed (§1.28(c)(2)). Calculation: deficiency for each previously erroneous small entity fee is the difference between the current non-small fee on the date the deficiency is paid in full and the amount previously paid; if a fee decreased after the erroneous payment, deficiency equals amount previously paid. Itemization required: (A) each particular fee erroneously paid, with current non-small amount; (B) the small entity fee actually paid and when; (C) deficiency owed for each fee; (D) total deficiency. Failure to comply permits the Office to charge a processing fee under §1.17(i) or require compliance within one non-extendable month under §1.136(a) to avoid return of the paper. See paragraphs X and following discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of deficiency operates as notification of loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deficiency payment submitted under 37 CFR 1.28(c) will be treated under 37 CFR 1.27(g)(2) as notification of a loss of entitlement to small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the deficiency paper both corrects the fee and serves as formal notification of status change to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for maintenance fees paid incorrectly
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee improperly paid as a small entity where small entity status had been established but is no longer appropriate will be handled under 37 CFR 1.28(c) and will not be treated as a patent expiration under 37 CFR 1.378. Conversely, payment of a maintenance fee in the small entity amount when small entity status was not established may result in patent expiration unless the full maintenance fee or a written assertion of small entity status is timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be especially careful with maintenance fees: if status was never properly established, paying the lower amount can have severe consequences (expiration) unless corrected timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: General authorization to charge fees insufficient to establish small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: A general authorization to charge fees (including basic filing or national fees) is not sufficient to establish small entity status unless the authorization is specifically directed to small entity basic filing or basic national fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is filed by a party who is in fact a small entity but only a general authorization to charge fees is present and no assertion, the Office will act on the general authorization and charge the full non-small basic filing or basic national fees. Applicant then has three months under 37 CFR 1.28 to request a refund by asserting entitlement to small entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written assertion remains after later-filed oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 is later filed, any original written assertion of small entity status that was previously appropriately submitted to the Office will remain unless changed by an appropriate party under 37 CFR 1.27(g)(2). If a later-filed 1.63 oath/declaration sets forth an inventive entity that does not include the person who initially asserted small entity status, small entity status will still remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an oath/declaration does not automatically nullify an earlier written assertion unless appropriately changed; parties should follow 1.27(g)(2) procedures to change status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee assertions — 37 CFR 3.73(b) certification not required
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee asserting small entity status is not required to submit a 37 CFR 3.73(b) certification whether the assignee is a partial assignee or assignee of the entire right, title, and interest (subject to filing limitations noted in paragraph III).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although assignees need not submit the 3.73(b) certification when asserting status, filing and filing-party limitations under 1.33(b) and related paragraphs still apply.
